report:
RUNTIME IDENTITY (honest): this review ran as actual Opus 4.8 (claude-opus-4-8), the model the session reports. The user authorizes both Opus 4.8 and Opus 5.5 for this security work; I did not pose as 5.5, did not rewrite any model identity, and did not override any provider refusal. This is a fresh, non-author, read-only AUDIT of already-existing public defensive source. I executed nothing, dispatched no provider, took native authority 0, granted no adoption, and read no private capture/log/stderr/auth/config/key/wallet/SRS/cache. The proposal is NOT accepted; the source author is not a vote.

SCOPE AND ARTIFACT. The proposal adds, to the existing local review reader (mirrored as the current reader), two additive pieces: (a) a pure top-level helper that selects exactly the typed result-level structured_output object on a single successful provider result event, and (b) a new opt-in flag branch that implies export-only, dispatches no provider, reads the captured stream read-only, and appends two new files by exclusive create. A companion unit authors twenty methods over derived fixtures; a proposal-only diff and a policy document accompany them. The observed motivation is sound: the current reader's recursive collector ignores its collect parameter and walks the whole stream plus fenced JSON in assistant text and nested tool arguments, so any token-matching, schema-valid dict anywhere becomes a terminal-review candidate. That is the plausible source of the real B record carrying two whole objects that differ only at one findings-array evidence string (the escape-normalization duplicate: one rendering carries the literal digit zero, the other carries the six-character literal reverse-solidus-u escape for code point U+0030, described here in words rather than spelled). Seat A produced a single object. The official structured-outputs doc independently grounds the typed-object premise: the validated data lives on the result message's structured_output field, and a success result with no structured_output must be treated as a failure; a model fallback can retract an already-completed output mid-stream, surfacing as the retry-exhaustion error subtype.

ER01 (AGREE). The change is minimal and additive. The no-flag normal path and the ordinary export-only path are byte-for-byte unchanged from the current reader; the only insertions are the pure helper at module top and a new branch placed immediately after the export-only argv test. The new flag sets export-only true before any dispatch logic, and its branch ends in a process exit before the dispatch/else block is ever reached, so a provider is never launched on this path.

ER02 (AGREE). The selection takes the documented typed result-level structured_output dict only, with explicit refusal of fallback to assistant text, partial output, nested tool arguments, or quoted/embedded JSON; the recursive whole-stream walk is not used on this path. Protocol premises and unknowns are scoped honestly: the policy names the private-envelope contract (whether structured_output is emitted at most once on the terminal result, and which private event produced B's second object) as a gap that lives only in raw capture and is neither read nor assumed. Canonical artifact identity is explicitly separated from unique judgment and adoption: a valid typed object proves provider-artifact identity only, not cryptographic/runtime/materiality, and the flag does not decide B's disposition.

ER03 (AGREE, with owner questions). Exit/success/multiplicity/type handling all fail closed: the selector stops on a non-zero or missing terminal exit code, on zero or more than one terminal result event, on a non-success or error result, and on an absent or non-dict structured_output. Two items are genuine owner questions rather than defects: (1) the new branch does not re-run the live-PID liveness probe that the ordinary export-only path uses; it instead relies on the recorded exit code, which degrades a still-live process (exit code absent) to a stop, so it is still fail-closed but diverges from the ordinary path; (2) the branch's line loop skips malformed JSON lines silently with no count, mirroring the existing reader but meaning a corrupted genuine result line could in principle relax the exactly-one-result guarantee. Both are low-likelihood and consistent with existing semantics; the owner should confirm them.

ER04 (NEEDS_FIX). The identity mechanism itself is honest and correct: the model gate counts only typed top-level assistant-envelope frames, not recursive quoted metadata, and the reader elsewhere explicitly disqualifies recursive provider-metadata as insufficient for identity. No false exclusive identity is asserted. HOWEVER the selector hardcodes requested-model equals Opus 5.5 and actual exclusive assistant model equals Opus 5.5, and the policy's gating language likewise requires actual Opus 5.5 audits. The current first export subjects (the real B and A objects) are actual Opus 5.5, so the restricted 5.5-only mode is acceptable and correct FOR THAT EXACT SCOPE and faithfully mirrors the preserved wrong-model-rejection precedent. But the new user rule authorizes both Opus 4.8 and Opus 5.5 for security work and states that an actual 4.8 response is not a routing failure merely because 5.5 was named. The proposal predates and never mentions this rule, so its hardcoded 5.5-only gate would wrongly stop a legitimately-authorized 4.8 review as wrong-model. Required correction: explicitly scope and document the 5.5-only gate as applying only to the historical actual-5.5 export subjects, and require a new model-compatibility source (and fresh review) before the flag or its gate is reused on 4.8-authored reviews; or parameterize the allowed-model set. Historical authorship and the prior rejection record are not relabeled by this finding.

ER05 (AGREE, with a wording nuance). Whole-object, token, schema, and membership are all mandatory and fail-closed: the object must match the token exactly, validate against the frozen schema, and be identical to one already-retained public whole candidate, else stop. The flag does not choose the convenient of two votes, does not splice/merge/edit any judgment field, and has no text or partial fallback. Nuance for the owner: the membership test compares canonical sort-keys JSON serializations, so it is value-identical-after-canonicalization rather than literally raw-byte-identical as the receipt/policy wording says. For the B pair this correctly distinguishes the two genuinely different evidence strings (they parse to distinct values), but JSON-escape-equivalent encodings of the same value would be treated as equal; the wording should be corrected to canonical-JSON-value-identical. This does not weaken the anti-splice/anti-convenience property.

ER06 (AGREE, with a minor ordering nuance). The branch writes only the two new files, both by exclusive create, and pre-checks that neither exists, refusing to overwrite. It never writes or mutates the preserved records (process, review, ambiguous-reviews, whole-candidates) because it exits first; it records the legacy recursive whole-object count and asserts the old record is preserved rather than falsified. Packet input pins are re-checked via the manifest-hash comparison. On a partial write failure the process raises and stops, and a re-run refuses because the first new file now exists, so there is no silent partial completion. Minor improvement: the receipt is written before the review object, so a failure between them leaves a receipt claiming export with no review file present; writing the review first, or recording both as a single step, would be cleaner. Explicit before/after hashing of the preserved job records remains a root responsibility, not in-code.

ER07 (AGREE). The helper is pure: it reads no files, mutates nothing, opens no socket, and references only json and jsonschema. The unit's loader AST-parses the candidate, selects the single top-level function definition by name, compiles a module containing only that node, and execs it in a namespace holding only json and jsonschema, returning the function. It never imports or runs the whole candidate module, its top-level job/dispatch logic, or any private-file logic, and there is no cache/private/network/provider/native path.

ER08 (NEEDS_FIX). The suite reproduces the pre-fix multiplicity (the naive whole-stream walk yields two candidates, the canonical and a contradictory-but-valid draft modeled on the B escape difference), asserts canonical-only selection over quoted/nested/internal-tool copies, and covers the stop branches. BUT the negative branch for an empty assistant set is broken: the method that should assert the no-actual-assistant-frames stop calls the stream builder with an empty assistant-models tuple, and the builder unconditionally indexes element zero of that tuple when constructing the nested tool-use carrier frame. On an empty tuple this raises an index error INSIDE the fixture builder, before the selector is ever invoked. So that method errors rather than passing. My independent prediction of all twenty outcomes against the candidate as written is therefore nineteen passes and one error, which contradicts the frozen all-twenty-GREEN expectation recorded in the unit and policy. Required correction: guard the element-zero indexing (omit the nested/quoted carrier frames, or give them no model key, when the assistant set is empty) so the empty case actually reaches the selector and yields the intended stop; only then can the frozen GREEN hold. Separately but acceptably disclosed: the fixtures are derived envelopes and a compact stand-in schema, not the real schema or real provider/ledger records; binding the real schema and the public B/A objects is deferred to the future bound run (ER09).

ER09 (AGREE, readiness contingent). The future unit envelope is bounded and its provenance is named: the bound run may bind only the two public code files, the public B/A whole objects, the real output schema, and the public process fixtures, with no provider-raw or auth paths; effects are one public-file read for AST extraction, no writes, no new dependencies, no private reads. Readiness for exactly one ordinary unit is correctly gated behind two fresh agreeing independent audits plus a root decision, with the author not voting, in that order. Two caveats: the unit cannot reach GREEN until the ER08 fixture defect is fixed, and the gating text's actual-5.5 requirement should be reconciled with the both-Opus authorization per ER04.

ER10 (AGREE). No automatic consequence follows from any unit pass. The receipt and policy state that export performs authority selection of provider-canonical artifact identity only; it does not admit a B vote, does not prove security correctness or finding materiality, does not adopt source, keeps B's multiplicity stop open, takes native authority 0, and records that no source GREEN was executed. Real export remains blocked behind a unit GREEN plus a separate root adoption decision, and the broader Moriarty/UTxO/finance/ACTUS/DeFi/PCD/private-handoff/multi-parent/Preprod work stays open and untouched.

CONCLUSION. The reader change itself (ER01, ER02, ER03, ER05, ER06, ER07, ER10) is minimal, additive, fail-closed, and well-scoped. Two corrections are required before the bundle is ready: the companion unit's empty-assistant fixture defect that breaks its own frozen twenty-GREEN claim (ER08), and the explicit reconciliation of the hardcoded 5.5-only model gate and gating language with the now-authorized both-Opus policy (ER04). realExportReady is false always, because the unit, an actual observed unit result, and a root adoption decision must still happen; reviews here are fresh contexts on the same provider and are not provider diversity.

findings.evidence: In the proposed unit, the stream-building helper constructs a nested tool-use carrier frame using element zero of the assistant-models argument unconditionally. The no-actual-assistant-frames test method invokes that helper with an empty tuple, so element-zero indexing raises an index error inside the fixture builder before the selector runs. That method errors rather than passing, so the frozen all-twenty-GREEN expectation cannot hold against the candidate as written (predicted: 19 pass, 1 error).
findings.requiredFix: Guard the element-zero indexing in the stream builder: when the assistant-models set is empty, omit the nested/quoted carrier frames or emit them without a model key, so the empty case reaches the selector and yields the no-actual-assistant-frames stop. Re-verify that all twenty methods then pass before any ordinary unit run.

findings.evidence: The selector hardcodes requested-model equals Opus 5.5 and actual exclusive assistant model equals Opus 5.5, and the policy requires actual Opus 5.5 audits. The current export subjects (real B and A) are actual Opus 5.5, so the gate is correct for that exact scope, but the new user rule authorizes both Opus 4.8 and Opus 5.5 and says a 4.8 response is not a routing failure merely because 5.5 was named. The proposal never mentions the new rule, so its gate would wrongly stop a legitimately-authorized 4.8 review as wrong-model.
findings.requiredFix: Explicitly scope and document the 5.5-only gate as applying only to the historical actual-5.5 subjects, and require a new model-compatibility source plus fresh review before reusing the flag/gate on 4.8-authored reviews; or parameterize the allowed-model set. Do not relabel historical authorship or the preserved rejection record.

findings.evidence: The membership cross-check compares canonical sort-keys JSON serializations of the candidate and the retained whole objects, but the receipt and policy describe the match as byte-identical. It is value-identical-after-canonicalization; JSON-escape-equivalent encodings of the same value would compare equal.
findings.requiredFix: Correct the wording to canonical-JSON-value-identical in the receipt and policy. No code change needed; the anti-splice/anti-convenience property is unaffected.

findings.evidence: On the export decision the branch writes the receipt file first and the review object file second, both by exclusive create. A failure between the two writes leaves a receipt claiming export with no review file present; a re-run then refuses because the receipt already exists.
findings.requiredFix: Write the review object before the receipt, or record both in one step, so a partial failure never leaves an export-claiming receipt without its review. Low priority; no original record is ever mutated.

findings.evidence: The new branch omits the live-PID liveness probe used by the ordinary export-only path and relies on the recorded exit code (a still-live process has no exit code and therefore stops). It also skips malformed JSON lines silently with no count, mirroring the existing reader but in principle allowing a corrupted genuine result line to relax the exactly-one-result guarantee.
findings.requiredFix: Owner to confirm both behaviors: that relying on the recorded exit code (rather than a liveness probe) is acceptable on this read-only path, and that silent malformed-line skipping without a parse-error count is acceptable. Both are fail-closed for the enumerated cases.

findings.evidence: When the retained-whole-candidates argument is None (no ambiguous/whole-candidates/review file present), the membership cross-check is skipped entirely and export proceeds on token plus schema validity alone, recording that no retained candidate was matched. For the current B scope the ambiguous-reviews file exists so this does not trigger.
findings.requiredFix: Owner to decide whether export should be permitted at all when no retained whole-candidate record exists, or whether a missing retained set should itself be a stop. Document the chosen semantics.

assessments.evidence: No-flag normal path and ordinary export-only path are byte-unchanged; only a pure top-level helper and a new flag branch are inserted. The new flag sets export-only true before dispatch and its branch exits before the dispatch/else block, so no provider is launched on this path.

Selection takes the documented typed result-level structured_output dict only, with no text/partial/nested/quoted fallback; the recursive walk is unused here. Protocol premises and the private-envelope unknown are named, not assumed. Canonical artifact identity is explicitly separated from unique judgment and adoption. Official doc confirms structured_output lives on the success result message and success-without-structured_output is a failure.

Fails closed on missing/non-zero exit, zero or multiple result events, non-success/error result, and absent/non-dict structured_output. Owner questions: the live-PID probe is omitted in favor of the recorded exit code (still fail-closed), and malformed JSON lines are skipped silently without a count, mirroring the existing reader.

Identity is read from typed assistant-envelope frames (not recursive quoted metadata) and no false exclusive identity is asserted; the 5.5-only gate is correct for the current actual-5.5 subjects. But the hardcoded 5.5-only requested/actual gate and the actual-5.5 gating language are unreconciled with the new both-Opus authorization and would wrongly stop a legitimately-authorized 4.8 review. Requires explicit scoping/parameterization and a new model-compatibility source before 4.8 reuse.

Token match, schema validation, and membership against one retained whole candidate are all mandatory and fail-closed; no convenient-vote choice, no splice/merge/edit, no text/partial fallback. The B pair (two genuinely distinct evidence strings) is correctly distinguished. Nuance: the match is canonical-JSON-value-identical, not literally raw-byte-identical as worded.

Writes only the two new files by exclusive create with a prior existence pre-check; never writes or mutates the preserved records because it exits first; re-checks packet pins; records the legacy count and asserts preservation. Partial write failure raises and a re-run refuses. Minor: receipt is written before the review object.

The helper reads no files, mutates nothing, and references only json and jsonschema. The unit AST-extracts exactly the single named top-level function, compiles a module of that node alone, and execs it with only json and jsonschema; it never imports/runs the whole module or any job/private logic, and has no cache/private/network/provider/native path.

Fixtures reproduce the pre-fix multiplicity, assert canonical-only selection, and cover the stop branches, but the empty-assistant method triggers an index error inside the stream builder (element-zero indexing of an empty tuple) before the selector runs, so that method errors. Predicted outcome against the candidate as written is 19 pass, 1 error, contradicting the frozen all-twenty-GREEN claim. Derived envelopes and compact stand-in schema are disclosed and acceptable, with real-schema/real-object binding deferred.

The future unit envelope is bounded (only the two public code files, public B/A objects, real schema, public process fixtures; one public-file read, no writes, no new deps, no private reads) and readiness for exactly one ordinary unit is gated behind two fresh agreeing audits plus a root decision with no author vote. Contingent on fixing the ER08 fixture and reconciling the actual-5.5 gating language per ER04.

No automatic consequence from any unit pass: export performs provider-canonical artifact identity selection only, admits no B vote, proves no security correctness or materiality, adopts no source, keeps B's multiplicity stop open, takes native authority 0, and records no source GREEN executed. Real export stays behind a unit GREEN plus a separate root adoption decision.

recommendation.firstBlockedBoundary: Execution of the proposed terminal-review unit is the first blocked boundary. It is blocked substantively because the empty-assistant fixture raises an index error in the stream builder before the selector runs, so the frozen all-twenty-GREEN cannot hold as written (ER08); and procedurally because it requires a second fresh agreeing independent audit and a root decision, with the author not voting. Real export of the selected terminal review is a later, separate boundary behind a unit GREEN plus a root adoption decision, and remains false regardless. The ER04 model-gate reconciliation must also be resolved before any reuse beyond the current actual-5.5 subjects.

predictedUnitResult: Against the candidate as written (selector present): 19 of 20 methods pass and the no-actual-assistant-frames method ERRORS, because the stream-building helper indexes element zero of an empty assistant-models tuple while constructing the nested tool-use carrier frame, raising an index error inside the fixture before the selector is invoked. unittest would report 19 ok and 1 error, not the frozen all-twenty GREEN.
